## Role in Plexus

- **Kind** &mdash; $\mathcal{O}_E$ **lateral**: within-set interaction over a relation $E$.
- **Acts on** &mdash; `particle` (the set the operator acts on).
- **Reads** &mdash; `cell_set`, `tension`
- **Writes / returns** &mdash; emits **no integrated force** &mdash; it mutates a field / relation / membership, or feeds a substep.
- **Prediction** &mdash; `none`.
- **Dimensions** &mdash; 2D, 3D.

## Mechanism

particle -[containment]-> particle: reads the cell's centre through the containment map, takes
the outward normal at each membrane point as the direction away from it, and writes

into the per-set `act_stress` buffer that `mpm_scatter` adds to the Kirchhoff stress. `gamma` is
a tension in the run's stress units; `I - m m^T` is the projector onto the surface, so the
stress is tangential -- a sheet pulled taut in its own plane, pulling on nothing along its
normal. On a curved sheet that is a net INWARD force of gamma times the curvature, which is
Laplace's law: a tension gamma balances an interior pressure P = 2 gamma / R, so a cell of
radius 14 um held against P = 43 wants a gamma of about 3.

WHY THIS IS THE PIECE THAT WAS MISSING, and why it is not a prescribed shape change. The target
-- adh_grow_all, measured on its own trajectory -- is 22.7 <-> 64.6 um in length WHILE the width
goes the other way, 31.1 <-> 19.3 um, at constant volume. Polymerisation cannot do that: it adds
volume, so it inflates. Depolymerisation cannot help, because removing points applies no force
any more than adding them does -- an emptied flank does not come in, and add-front/remove-back
merely treadmills (28.0 -> 28.9 um while the cell translates). Something has to PULL, and in a
cell that something is the actomyosin cortex.

Nothing here is directional. The tension is the same at every point of the membrane, and the
normal it uses is the cell's own geometry rather than its polarity. The elongation, if it
appears, comes from the INTERACTION: material arrives at the leading edge and pushes there while
the cortex squeezes everywhere it is not being pushed. The front-back asymmetry is supplied by
the polymerisation; the cortex supplies only the constraint that the cell cannot get fatter for
free. That is the biological division of labour -- protrusion sets the direction, contraction
sets the shape -- and it is why both belong in the run rather than one being tuned to imitate
the other.

THE SIGN. A POSITIVE stress pulls material together in this solver -- `mpm_turgor` writes a
pressure that is SUBTRACTED from the stress in order to push outward -- so a tension is entered
positive and a pressure negative. `tension` is therefore a plain positive number.

Reference: Salbreux, G., Charras, G. & Paluch, E. (2012). Actin cortex mechanics and cellular
morphogenesis. Trends Cell Biol. 22:536-545; Clark, A. G., Wartlick, O., Salbreux, G. & Paluch,
E. K. (2014). Stresses at the cell surface during animal cell morphogenesis. Curr. Biol.
24:R484-R494.

## Source

[`src/plexus/operators/cell_ops.py`](https://github.com/allierc/Plexus/blob/main/src/plexus/operators/cell_ops.py) &mdash; the registered operator.

```python
@register_operator("cortical_tension", family="motility", set="particle", kind="lateral")
class CorticalTension(Lateral):
    """The cortex pulling in: an IN-PLANE tension on the membrane, isotropic and undirected.

    particle -[containment]-> particle: reads the cell's centre through the containment map, takes
    the outward normal at each membrane point as the direction away from it, and writes

        sigma_cortex = gamma (I - m m^T),      m = (x - c) / |x - c|

    into the per-set `act_stress` buffer that `mpm_scatter` adds to the Kirchhoff stress. `gamma` is
    a tension in the run's stress units; `I - m m^T` is the projector onto the surface, so the
    stress is tangential -- a sheet pulled taut in its own plane, pulling on nothing along its
    normal. On a curved sheet that is a net INWARD force of gamma times the curvature, which is
    Laplace's law: a tension gamma balances an interior pressure P = 2 gamma / R, so a cell of
    radius 14 um held against P = 43 wants a gamma of about 3.

    WHY THIS IS THE PIECE THAT WAS MISSING, and why it is not a prescribed shape change. The target
    -- adh_grow_all, measured on its own trajectory -- is 22.7 <-> 64.6 um in length WHILE the width
    goes the other way, 31.1 <-> 19.3 um, at constant volume. Polymerisation cannot do that: it adds
    volume, so it inflates. Depolymerisation cannot help, because removing points applies no force
    any more than adding them does -- an emptied flank does not come in, and add-front/remove-back
    merely treadmills (28.0 -> 28.9 um while the cell translates). Something has to PULL, and in a
    cell that something is the actomyosin cortex.

    Nothing here is directional. The tension is the same at every point of the membrane, and the
    normal it uses is the cell's own geometry rather than its polarity. The elongation, if it
    appears, comes from the INTERACTION: material arrives at the leading edge and pushes there while
    the cortex squeezes everywhere it is not being pushed. The front-back asymmetry is supplied by
    the polymerisation; the cortex supplies only the constraint that the cell cannot get fatter for
    free. That is the biological division of labour -- protrusion sets the direction, contraction
    sets the shape -- and it is why both belong in the run rather than one being tuned to imitate
    the other.

    THE SIGN. A POSITIVE stress pulls material together in this solver -- `mpm_turgor` writes a
    pressure that is SUBTRACTED from the stress in order to push outward -- so a tension is entered
    positive and a pressure negative. `tension` is therefore a plain positive number.

    Reference: Salbreux, G., Charras, G. & Paluch, E. (2012). Actin cortex mechanics and cellular
    morphogenesis. Trends Cell Biol. 22:536-545; Clark, A. G., Wartlick, O., Salbreux, G. & Paluch,
    E. K. (2014). Stresses at the cell surface during animal cell morphogenesis. Curr. Biol.
    24:R484-R494.
    """
    EMIT = None                       # a stress, consumed by the substep; no integrable delta
    SUPPORTED_DIMS = [2, 3]
    DIFFERENTIABLE = True
    REQUIRES_PARAMS = ["cell_set", "tension"]
    INPUTS = ["particle", "cell"]; OUTPUTS = ["particle"]
    READS = []; WRITES = []
    MAPS = ["parent"]
    MECHANISM_TAGS = ["cortical_tension", "contractility", "surface_tension", "morphogenesis"]
    PARAM_ROLES = {"tension": "in_plane_cortical_tension", "cell_set": "cell_owner",
                   "mode": "stress_form",
                   "gate": "phase_gate"}
    REFERENCE = ("Salbreux, G., Charras, G. & Paluch, E. (2012). Trends Cell Biol. 22:536-545; "
                 "Clark, A. G. et al. (2014). Curr. Biol. 24:R484-R494.")

    def __init__(self, params, device="cpu"):
        super().__init__(params, device)
        self.at = params.get("_at", "particle")
        self.cell_set = str(params["cell_set"])
        self.tension = float(params["tension"])
        # HOW THE CONTRACTION IS CARRIED, and it is not a matter of taste but of what the set IS.
        #   tangential  sigma = gamma (I - m m^T): a sheet pulled taut in its own plane. Correct for
        #               a CONNECTED cortex, and useless on this cell's membrane, which is 421
        #               separate patches: a tangential stress needs a continuous sheet for its
        #               divergence to be the Laplace force, and across disconnected patches that
        #               divergence is nearly zero. Measured, gamma 3 and gamma 12 gave the SAME
        #               trajectory to two decimals, and gamma 500 gave NaN -- no useful range at all.
        #   isotropic   sigma = gamma I on a dense, connected region: the region wants to shrink, and
        #               at its boundary that is a net inward force. This is what to put on the
        #               cytoskeleton -- 240,000 points filling a shell, which is the actomyosin
        #               network the contraction physically belongs to -- and it competes with the
        #               crowding pressure in the same units, so the front wins exactly where
        #               material is arriving and the flanks lose everywhere else.
        self.mode = str(params.get("mode", "tangential"))
        self.gate = params.get("gate")
        self._said = False

    def forward(self, H, mask=None):
        p = H.level(self.at)
        cl = H.level(self.cell_set)
        X = p.get("pos")
        D = X.shape[1]
        idx = H.lift_index(p.name, self.cell_set)
        c0 = cl.state_schema["pos"][0]
        rel = X[:, :D] - cl.state[idx, c0:c0 + D]
        m = rel / rel.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
        eye = torch.eye(D, device=X.device, dtype=X.dtype)[None]
        g = torch.as_tensor(self.tension, device=X.device, dtype=X.dtype).expand(p.n).clone()
        gt = _gate(self, H, idx)
        if gt is not None:
            g = g * gt
        if mask is not None:
            g = g * mask.float()
        occ = getattr(p, "occ", None)
        if occ is not None:
            g = g * (occ > 0).to(g.dtype)
        # THE SIGN, FROM THE CONSTITUTIVE LAW RATHER THAN FROM AN EXPERIMENT AT THE WRONG SCALE.
        # A compressed neo-Hookean material has lambda (J - 1) J < 0 and must push outward, so a
        # NEGATIVE isotropic stress is a pressure and a POSITIVE one is a tension that pulls in --
        # which is also why `turgor`, whose job is to push out, is SUBTRACTED from the stress.
        # Both signs appear to "expand" the cell if they are large enough (3,000 sent the membrane
        # from a radius of 10.4 um to 25.8 and then back to 19.5): that is an instability
        # oscillating, not a response, and a sign cannot be read off it.
        sig = g[:, None, None] * (eye if self.mode == "isotropic"
                                  else (eye - m[:, :, None] * m[:, None, :]))
        buf = getattr(p, "act_stress", None)
        if buf is None or buf.shape != sig.shape:
            p.register_buffer("act_stress", torch.zeros_like(sig))
            buf = p.act_stress
        buf.copy_(sig)
        if not self._said:
            self._said = True
            r = float(rel.norm(dim=1).median())
            print(f"[cortical_tension] {self.at}: gamma {self.tension:g} on a cortex of radius "
                  f"{r:.4g} -- it balances an interior pressure of "
                  f"{2 * self.tension / max(r, 1e-9):.3g}", flush=True)
        return {}
```
